speaker: Ryan Lopopolo
en: Yeah.

en: A lot of fancy context management techniques in order to get these agents to learn from their own mistakes, produce high quality code, and go for a very long time without human intervention.

speaker: Guy Fajani
en: Absolutely.

speaker: Guy Fajani
en: And we're gonna talk about harness engineering, and we'll talk about some of the methodologies that you've used internally at OpenAI and talk through maybe some of the bits that have been enjoyable, some of the bits that have been scary, and it's gonna be great fun.
zh: 我们将谈论 harness 工程，我们将谈论你在 OpenAI 内部使用的一些方法，并讨论其中一些有趣的片段，一些可怕的片段，这将会非常有趣。

speaker: Guy Fajani
en: So, Ryan, why don't we kick off with harness engineering?
zh: 那么，Ryan，我们为什么不从 harness 工程开始呢？

speaker: Guy Fajani
en: For the layman, what is harness engineering?
zh: 对于外行来说，什么是 harness 工程？

speaker: Ryan Lopopolo
en: Yeah, so we have these wonderful technology and these coding agents and these fantastic models that are very smart and able to produce a ton of code.
zh: 是的，所以我们有这些美妙的技术和这些编码智能体以及这些非常智能并能产生大量代码的奇妙模型。

speaker: Ryan Lopopolo
en: Uh and harness engineering is this idea that to produce code that is acceptable, to produce code that we trust, that we can build confidence in business systems around, there are a bunch of little decisions that go into the process of producing PRs, producing systems that we have to make along the way.
zh: harness 工程就是这个想法，为了产生可接受的代码，产生我们信任的代码，我们可以围绕其建立业务系统的信心，有一堆小决策进入了产生 PR 的过程，产生我们在沿途必须制作的系统。

speaker: Ryan Lopopolo
en: And in order to get the agent to know and understand those, we have to write it down.
zh: 为了让智能体知道并理解那些，我们必须把它们写下来。

speaker: Ryan Lopopolo
en: We have to make sure that like the content of those choices, all those non-functional requirements that go into making good code get surfaced to the agent at the right time.
zh: 我们必须确保这些选择的内容，所有那些进入优秀代码的非功能性需求，在正确的时间暴露给智能体。

speaker: Ryan Lopopolo
en: So it's a combination of getting context into the repository in a place where these coding agents can see it, surfacing it to the agent at the right time, and making sure that all the code that we produce kind of like follows the golden thread of what it means for us to produce high-quality software.
zh: 所以这是一种将上下文放入这些编码智能体可以看到的存储库中的组合，在正确的时间将其暴露给智能体，并确保我们产生的所有代码都遵循我们要产生高质量软件的金线。

speaker: Ryan Lopopolo
en: Reviewer agents, tests, lints, uh big refactoring loops, all sort of ways to get the agent to close the loop and make sure that uh it proves to me and the rest of the team that the code it has produced is acceptable and can't be merged.
zh: 审查智能体、测试、lints、大的重构循环，所有这些方式都是为了智能体能够闭环，并确保它向我和其他团队证明它产生的代码是可接受的并且不能被合并。

speaker: Guy Fajani
en: So we've had prompt engineering, context engineering, and harness engineering now.
zh: 所以我们现在有了提示词工程、上下文工程和 harness 工程。

speaker: Guy Fajani
en: What would you say are the kind of like the main differences or overlap between context engineering and harness engineering?
zh: 你会说上下文工程和 harness 工程之间的主要区别或重叠是什么？

speaker: Ryan Lopopolo
en: I think really the two only levers you have when interacting with agents is which context you provide and which tools you provide.
zh: 我认为实际上你与智能体交互时仅有的两个杠杆是你提供什么上下文和你提供什么工具。

speaker: Ryan Lopopolo
en: And harness engineering is kind of a combination of both with the goal of making sure the context that we give the agent is correct so that it can work its reasoning magic to produce good code.
zh: harness 工程是两者的结合，目标是我们给智能体的上下文是正确的，这样它可以发挥它的推理魔法来产生好的代码。

speaker: Ryan Lopopolo
en: And one thing that I think is unique about harness engineering is we're actually using the tool calls themselves to prompt inject the agent to manage its context window.
zh: 我认为 harness 工程独特的一点是，我们实际上使用工具调用来提示词注入智能体以管理其上下文窗口。

speaker: Ryan Lopopolo
en: One thing that's pretty neat here is the way that we structure tests and lints and well-formed tests in the code base is actually very different than how I would structure those messages for a human, right?
zh: 这里有一件很整洁的事情是，我们在代码库中构建测试和 lints 以及格式良好的测试的方式实际上与我为人类构建那些消息的方式非常不同，对吧？

speaker: Ryan Lopopolo
en: I would have an exhaustive list of failures that I give the human and have them wade through the logs in order to figure out what's wrong.
zh: 我会有一份详尽的失败列表给人类，让他们在日志中跋涉以找出问题所在。

speaker: Ryan Lopopolo
en: Whereas with agents, you know, due to the nature of how they invoke tools, we want those messages to be somewhat compressed, but also semantically meaningful, right?
zh: 而对于智能体，你知道，由于它们调用工具的性质，我们希望这些消息在一定程度上被压缩，但在语义上也是有意义的，对吧？

speaker: Ryan Lopopolo
en: Rather than giving sort of a mechanical ESLint failure, for example, I can give a prose error message that says, you screwed it up in this way in this file.
zh: 与其给出那种机械性的 ESLint 失败，例如，我可以给出一整段文字的错误信息，说，你在这个文件里是以这种方式搞砸的。

speaker: Ryan Lopopolo
en: You know, please open it and follow the runbook in file XYZ to go fix it.
zh: 你知道，请打开它并遵循文件 XYZ 里的运行手册去修复它。

speaker: Ryan Lopopolo
en: Because we've seen you make this mistake before, and we know that we can trust you to do the right thing.
zh: 因为我们见过你以前犯过这个错误，而且我们知道我们可以信任你做正确的事。

speaker: Guy Fajani
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Guy Fajani
en: And that that that level of integration, that deeper integration, really unlocks that next step, right?
zh: 而那种那种那种程度的集成，那种更深度的集成，真的解锁了下一步，对吧？

speaker: Guy Fajani
en: Um now interesting, I'm looking I'm like looking at some of the uh some of your background here.
zh: 嗯现在有趣的是，我正在看，我就像在看一些你的背景资料。

speaker: Guy Fajani
en: You built Stripe's efficiency engineering team, led developer productivity at BREX for 350 engineers.

speaker: Guy Fajani
en: There's a bunch of kind of like infrastructure and DX background there.

speaker: Guy Fajani
en: Would you say that helped you or hindered you from the point of view of harness engineering?
zh: 你会说这从驾驭工程的角度来说是有助于你还是阻碍了你吗？

speaker: Ryan Lopopolo
en: Uh definitely helped.
zh: 呃肯定是有帮助的。

speaker: Ryan Lopopolo
en: It kind of uh got me used to this idea of working through others.
zh: 它有点呃让我习惯了这种通过他人来工作的想法。

speaker: Ryan Lopopolo
en: Uh, you know, when I'm trying to improve productivity for an engineering organization of 350 engineers, I can't be hands-on in the weeds of every PR that's being produced.
zh: 呃，你知道，当我试图为 350 人的工程组织提高生产力时，我无法亲力亲为深入每一个正在生成的 PR 的细节。

speaker: Ryan Lopopolo
en: And I can't work directly on the underlying systems.
zh: 而且我也无法直接在底层系统上工作。

speaker: Ryan Lopopolo
en: I kind of have to steer from the background, make sure that the right things are happening by default, the right systems are in place in order to have high trust in the organization to do good work.
zh: 我有点必须要在幕后掌舵，确保默认情况下发生正确的事情，正确的系统已到位，以便对组织做高质量工作拥有高度的信任。

speaker: Ryan Lopopolo
en: And that's exactly what it means in order to be high functioning with these agents.
zh: 而这正是要高效运作这些智能体所意味着的。

speaker: Ryan Lopopolo
en: In order to move beyond sort of coding agents as pair programming assistants to go massively parallel where I've got the 15 TMUX windows open, I need to be able to take my hands off the wheel to a certain extent.
zh: 为了超越那种将编码智能体作为结对编程助手的情况，走向大规模并行，在那儿我有 15 个 TMUX 窗口开着，我需要能够在一定程度上放手。

speaker: Ryan Lopopolo
en: So, this way of operating, this sort of systems thinking mentality kind of comes pretty naturally to me because that's kind of the expertise I've had to build up over the course of my career.
zh: 所以，这种操作方式，这种系统思维心态对我来说很自然，因为那是我不得不在整个职业生涯中建立起来的专业知识。

speaker: Guy Fajani
en: Yeah, yeah, interesting.
zh: 是，是，有趣。

speaker: Guy Fajani
en: We'll actually touch a little bit about, I guess, the the part of that which is, well, how much is how much trust do you need then to have those 15 open?

en: But we'll cover that in just a second.

en: It was definitely a bit of a radical idea at the time.

speaker: Ryan Lopopolo
en: Um kind of when I started out uh building in this way was uh even before we had proper reasoning models, GPT 5 came out in August of 2025, and I started working in this hands-off way in June.

speaker: Ryan Lopopolo
en: Uh so this is you know 03 era Codex Mini had just came out, the very first versions of Codex CLI.
zh: 呃所以这是你知道 03 时代的 Codex Mini 刚刚出来，Codex CLI 的最早版本。

speaker: Ryan Lopopolo
en: And uh to be honest, back then the models were way less capable.
zh: 还有呃老实说，那时候模型的能力要差得多。

speaker: Ryan Lopopolo
en: Uh it was very painful in order to operate hands-off like this.
zh: 呃为了像这样不插手操作是非常痛苦的。

speaker: Ryan Lopopolo
en: Um and sort of by necessity, working with the model, working with the coding agent, I kind of had to stick myself in as a very chunky tool uh for the model to delegate to.
zh: 嗯还有某种程度上出于必要，与模型合作，与编码智能体合作，我有点不得不把自己插进去作为一个非常笨重的工具呃供模型委派给。

speaker: Ryan Lopopolo
en: If it got stuck or if it needed to do something, the only thing it could do at the beginning was ask Ryan to do something for it.

speaker: Ryan Lopopolo
en: Uh eventually I get tired of being asked the same thing all the time.
zh: 呃最终我厌倦了总是被问同样的事情。

speaker: Ryan Lopopolo
en: Initially, back then it was um installing dependencies with cargo.
zh: 最初，那时候它是嗯用 cargo 安装依赖。

speaker: Ryan Lopopolo
en: This is just not something that uh that Codex was able to do reliably back then.
zh: 这只是某些东西呃 Codex 那时候无法可靠地做到。

speaker: Ryan Lopopolo
en: So I would type the commands in my terminal and you know, give the agent some dependencies to work with.
zh: 所以我会在我的终端里输入命令然后你知道，给智能体一些依赖来处理。

speaker: Ryan Lopopolo
en: And sort of automating that was the first step.
zh: 还有某种程度上自动化那是第一步。

speaker: Ryan Lopopolo
en: And it kind of got me in this mode of paying very close attention to where I'm spending my time, figuring out ways to build up a tool call that removes the need for me to spend that time.
zh: 而且它有点让我进入这种模式，非常密切地关注我花时间的地方，想办法建立一个工具调用来消除我花那时间的需要。

speaker: Ryan Lopopolo
en: So then I can kind of figure out the other ways that I can help the agent get more and more chunky tools to give it more capability.
zh: 所以然后我可以有点弄清楚其他方式让我能帮助智能体获得越来越多的笨重工具来给它更多能力。

speaker: Ryan Lopopolo
en: And to start with zero like that, you kind of viscerally experience the failure of the agent.
zh: 而像那样从零开始，你有点发自内心地体验智能体的失败。

speaker: Ryan Lopopolo
en: Uh I think to kind of have a good sense of the tool calls as they are making, the mistakes the agent is making sort of in the process of writing the code is really, really important in order to build confidence in it.
zh: 呃我认为有点对工具调用有一个好的感觉，正如它们正在进行的那样，智能体正在犯的错误某种程度上在写代码的过程中是真正，真正重要的以便建立对它的信心。

speaker: Ryan Lopopolo
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Ryan Lopopolo
en: Because to see what mistakes it's making, I'm also able to see the parts that it does really good at and can start to retool the way I go about my week to lean into the stuff Codex is really good at.
zh: 因为为了看到它在犯什么错，我也能看到它做得真正好的部分，并且可以开始重新调整我这一周的工作方式，以便深入利用 Codex 真正擅长的东西。

speaker: Ryan Lopopolo
en: It's really good at following instructions.

speaker: Ryan Lopopolo
en: It's really good at writing tests and calling them.
zh: 它真的非常擅长编写测试和调用它们。

speaker: Ryan Lopopolo
en: So collapsing a lot of the engineering process into these like very well-paved roads for the agent helps me build confidence in it.
zh: 所以把大量的工程过程折叠成这些像为智能体铺设得非常好的道路有助于我建立对它的信心。

speaker: Guy Fajani
en: It's funny how you say it's it's really good at following instructions and really and really good at writing tests.

speaker: Guy Fajani
en: And I'm thinking, wow, the complete opposite of most developers.

speaker: Guy Fajani
en: Is that is that maybe that's wrong to say?
zh: 是那是是也许那是错误的说法吗？

speaker: Guy Fajani
en: Um, but so that's really interesting.
zh: 嗯，所以那真的很有趣。

en: I got very lucky that as we grew the team, we grew it uh all with new hires to the company.
